- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >85.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after forecast peak, model may be lagging — adjust forecast to reflect earlier mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop — increase downward bias or add early correction factor.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak — reduce forecast magnitude by 3–5% for low-sentiment periods.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it — apply “mean reversion” correction: forecast = prior 5-day average + 10% downward adjustment.
- For sentiment history with multiple 0.4–0.6 spikes, model overreacts — cap forecast at 85.0–86.0 and reduce slope after 3rd spike.
